name: Police state
summary: A police state is a regime type rather than a doctrine: dictionaries and scholarship define it as a state in which the police, above all a secret police, exercise arbitrary and repressive control over political, economic and social life in place of publicly known legal procedure. The label is mostly a critic's description of regimes; the sources record no programme or thinkers who advocate it, so only the positions built into the definition can be answered.

topic/police-state page, 403 on direct fetch and 404 in the Wayback Machine

scope: The modern sense given by Merriam-Webster and Collins: a state that holds control by repressive, arbitrary police power, especially secret police, in place of regular legal procedure. It follows the dictionaries and Chapman's 1968 account; it excludes the 18th-century German Polizeistaat as a regulating welfare administration (Foucault, Chapman) except as the term's origin, and it takes no positions from particular regimes labelled police states, which are other subjects.
